rule: INACCESSIBLE is only written after every route returned a real HTTP result. A metadata flag never short-circuits a fetch: Europe PMC reported isOpenAccess=N and 404 for a deposit efetch served in full at 44,181 characters.

findings_2026_08_28.scope: 74 distinct trials across the 26 indexed topics; 74 attempted, 0 skipped
findings_2026_08_28.recovered: 74/74 trials hold at least the registration and 73 hold a PubMed record; 24 hold full text; 245 documents, 19.1 MB
findings_2026_08_28.the_big_win: 55 of 74 PMIDs were recovered FROM THE REGISTRATION. Only 18 were stored on the objects, so the number of trials linkable to a paper roughly TRIPLED without any search -- the identifier was already in a document we hold.
findings_2026_08_28.the_never_trust_rule_did_NOT_pay_off_the: 50 Europe PMC records declare isOpenAccess=N. Of those, ZERO yielded full text on any other route -- the index was RIGHT about full-text availability in all 50. What trying anyway did recover is an abstract-level PubMed record for 49 of the 50. The rule stands (a flag must never short-circuit a fetch, and one deposit elsewhere was served in full after a 404) but on THIS corpus it overturned no closed flag, and reporting it as though it had would be the flattering version of the result.
findings_2026_08_28.honest_failure: 12 of 36 PMC attempts returned no deposited full text. That is a real HTTP result on a tried route, not an inference from a flag.
findings_2026_08_28.one_trial_has_no_pmid: NCT01780987 -- no reference on its registration and none stored
